Tim and Geli Harris have spent more than a decade fighting to protect Catfield Fen, a rare wetland in the Norfolk Broads

Polluters and regulators who fail to stop pollution must quake in their boots when they receive a letter from the lawyers for Tim and Geli Harris. The couple, who farm 460 acres in the Norfolk Broads, have now scored a hat-trick of landmark legal victories to save an internationally important wetland after they won again in the high court this month.

Lady Justice Lieven found that Natural England failed in its statutory duty to protect Catfield Fen from pollution after nitrates and phosphates washed from arable fields into one of the finest examples of calcareous fen in western Europe, home to 2,500 species including rarities such as the fen orchid, crested buckler fern, breeding bittern and swallowtail butterflies.

A little before lunchtime each working day across Spain, evidence of one of the lingering, if less notorious, legacies of the Franco dictatorship is carefully traced in chalk, marker pen and printer ink.

items.title: As a divided Israel prepares to go to the polls, can Netanyahu pull off his greatest political trick yet?

The prime minister has defined and dominated his country’s politics for three decades and is putting his rivals on the defensive before Tuesday’s general election

They chant his name, they cheer and clap – and yet he is not the most dominant person in the room. Looming over the crowd that has gathered to hear Gadi Eisenkot, the former general who is the lead opposition challenger in Tuesday’s Israeli election, is a man who is not there. It is the man Eisenkot seeks to replace as prime minister, the man who first served in that role three decades ago and who has held it, on and off, for 19 of the past 30 years. It is Benjamin Netanyahu.

Naturally, the warm-up speakers at this evening rally in the modest city of Modi’in, halfway between Tel Aviv and Jerusalem, stress the virtues of Eisenkot, a son of working-class Moroccan Jews who rose through the ranks to become chief of staff of the Israel Defense Forces and entered politics only four years ago. items.title: Gabriel Dia à AKAA : l'art, les tabous et l'homosexualité au Sénégal
items.content_html:
À Paris, la foire d'art contemporain africain AKAA accueille une installation monumentale du photographe sénégalais Gabriel Dia. Avec Mother's Heritage, l'artiste revisite ses souvenirs d'enfance dans l'atelier de couture de sa mère, à Rufisque. Des photographies imprimées sur des tissus suspendus pour raconter la transmission, les interdits et la liberté d'être soi.

De son parcours dans l'ingénierie nucléaire à ses séries photographiques Sabar et Mother's Heritage, Gabriel Dia revient sur une œuvre profondément personnelle, qui interroge les normes de genre et les identités. Un travail qui prend une résonance particulière au Sénégal, où une loi promulguée en mars 2026 a considérablement durci les sanctions contre les relations homosexuelles.

Gabriel Dia est l'invité de Fatimata Wane dans le Journal de l'Afrique sur France 24, à l'occasion de la 11e édition d'AKAA, organisée du 23 au 25 octobre 2026 au Carreau du Temple, à Paris.
